context: Today you volunteer on a vegetable farm. Lots of new words, and your host talks fast while working.

phrases.jp: {何|なに}を{植|う}えるんですか。

phrases.note: {軍手|ぐんて} are the white cotton work gloves you see everywhere.

phrases.jp: {草|くさ}を{抜|ぬ}けばいいですか。
ちょっと{休憩|きゅうけい}してもいいですか。
phrases.en: Can I take a short break?

phrases.note: Every farmer says it. Instant bonding.

dialogue_setting: In a daikon field on a cold morning.

dialogue.speaker: Farmer
dialogue.jp: {今日|きょう}は{大根|だいこん}を{収穫|しゅうかく}するよ。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: どうやって{抜|ぬ}けばいいですか。
dialogue.en: How should I pull them out?

dialogue.speaker: Farmer
dialogue.jp: {葉|は}っぱの{根元|ねもと}を{持|も}って、まっすぐ{上|うえ}に{引|ひ}っ{張|ぱ}るの。
dialogue.en: Hold the base of the leaves and pull straight up.

dialogue.speaker: Farmer
dialogue.jp: そうそう！{上手|じょうず}じゃん。
dialogue.en: Yes, yes! You're good at this.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {思|おも}ったより{重|おも}いですね！

kanji.where: Along country roads, where farmers sell their own vegetables. Unmanned ones ({無人|むじん}) have a box for your coins.
kanji.related: Related: {産直|さんちょく} direct from the farm.

tip.title: Farm Japanese is casual
tip.body: Older farmers often use dialect and short casual forms: やるか (let's do it), {休|やす}もう (let's rest). If you miss something, repeat the key word as a question, like {大根|だいこん}？, and they'll show you. Lunch with the family is part of the job.

challenge.prompt: You're tired and thirsty. Ask the farmer: "Can I take a short break and drink some water?"
challenge.hint: drink water = {水|みず}を{飲|の}む, + ～てもいいですか
challenge.model_answer: ちょっと{休憩|きゅうけい}して、{水|みず}を{飲|の}んでもいいですか。
